name: UIStroke
simple: A UIStroke draws an outline. Put it in a Frame or button and it outlines the border; put it in a TextLabel and it outlines the letters. You can pick the color, thickness and transparency, and it follows rounded UICorner corners too.
analogy: A UIStroke is like tracing around a sticker with a marker, or outlining your bubble letters so they pop off the page.
whenToUse: Bold outlined text that's readable on any background
A glowing or colored border around a selected item
Rainbow outlines (add a UIGradient inside the UIStroke)
where: Put it inside the UI object to outline (Frame, TextLabel, TextButton, ImageLabel...). Create in Studio or with Instance.new in a LocalScript.

terms.modifier: A small invisible object you put INSIDE a UI object to change how it looks or behaves. It does nothing on its own.
terms.parent: The object something is placed inside. A modifier affects its parent.
terms.sibling: Objects that share the same parent, like brothers and sisters.
terms.UDim: Half of a UDim2: just one Scale and one Offset. UDim.new(0, 8) means 0% + 8 pixels. UDim.new(0.1, 0) means 10% of the parent's size.
terms.Scale: A fraction (0 to 1) of the parent's size. 0.5 = half.
terms.pixel: One tiny dot on the screen.
terms.LocalScript: A script that runs on the player's own device. UI code goes in LocalScripts.
terms.Vector2: Two numbers together: X (width or left-right) and Y (height or up-down).
terms.Color3: A color made of red, green and blue amounts.
terms.line join: The shape of the outline at a corner: round, cut off (bevel), or pointy (miter).
terms.tween: Smoothly animate a value from one number to another.
terms.beta: A test feature you may need to turn on in Studio before it works.

examples.title: Outlined text and an outlined rounded button
examples.code:
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local playerGui = Players.LocalPlayer:WaitForChild("PlayerGui")

local screenGui = Instance.new("ScreenGui")
screenGui.Parent = playerGui

-- Outlined title text
local title = Instance.new("TextLabel")
title.Size = UDim2.fromOffset(400, 80)
title.Position = UDim2.fromOffset(20, 20)
title.BackgroundTransparency = 1
title.Text = "MEGA OBBY"
title.TextSize = 60
title.TextColor3 = Color3.fromRGB(255, 220, 0)
title.Parent = screenGui

local textStroke = Instance.new("UIStroke")
textStroke.Thickness = 3
textStroke.Color = Color3.fromRGB(0, 0, 0)
textStroke.Parent = title -- outlines the LETTERS

-- Outlined rounded button
local button = Instance.new("TextButton")
button.Size = UDim2.fromOffset(200, 50)
button.Position = UDim2.fromOffset(20, 120)
button.Text = "Start"
button.Parent = screenGui

Instance.new("UICorner").Parent = button

local border = Instance.new("UIStroke")
border.ApplyStrokeMode = Enum.ApplyStrokeMode.Border -- outline the BOX, not the text
border.Thickness = 2
border.Color = Color3.fromRGB(0, 170, 255)
border.Parent = button
explain: A UIStroke inside a TextLabel outlines the text by default (ApplyStrokeMode Contextual).
On the button we set ApplyStrokeMode to Border so the outline goes around the box instead of the word.
Because the button also has a UICorner, the outline follows the rounded corners.

gotchas: On text objects, the stroke outlines the letters unless ApplyStrokeMode is Border.
Animating Thickness on text can be slow and flicker; avoid tweening it on text.
Several UIStrokes with the same ZIndex draw in an unpredictable order; give them different ZIndex values.
Some newer properties (BorderOffset, BorderStrokePosition, StrokeSizingMode) may need the Improved UIStrokes beta.

UIStroke.ApplyStrokeMode.simple: For text objects: Contextual (default) outlines the letters, Border outlines the box around them. On a Frame it always outlines the border.
UIStroke.ApplyStrokeMode.example:
local stroke = script.Parent -- a UIStroke inside a TextButton
stroke.ApplyStrokeMode = Enum.ApplyStrokeMode.Border

UIStroke.BorderOffset.simple: Pushes the outline in or out from where it would normally be, as a UDim. Offset is pixels (negative moves it inward). Scale is a fraction of the parent's smaller side. UDim.new(0, -16) pulls the outline 16 pixels inside the edge.
UIStroke.BorderOffset.example:
local stroke = script.Parent
stroke.BorderOffset = UDim.new(0, 4) -- 4 px further out

UIStroke.BorderStrokePosition.simple: Where the outline sits on the edge: Outer (outside the edge), Center (half in, half out) or Inner (inside the edge).

UIStroke.Color.simple: The outline's color. Put a UIGradient inside the UIStroke to make a multi-color outline.
UIStroke.Color.example:
local stroke = script.Parent
stroke.Color = Color3.fromRGB(255, 0, 0) -- red outline

UIStroke.Enabled.simple: Turns the outline on (true, default) or off (false) without deleting it. Handy for showing which item is selected.

UIStroke.LineJoinMode.simple: The shape of the outline at corners: Round (default, smooth), Bevel (cut flat) or Miter (sharp point).

UIStroke.StrokeSizingMode.simple: Whether Thickness is measured in pixels (FixedSize, the default) or as a fraction of the parent's size (ScaledSize), so the outline grows with the object.
UIStroke.StrokeSizingMode.example:
local stroke = script.Parent
stroke.StrokeSizingMode = Enum.StrokeSizingMode.ScaledSize
stroke.Thickness = 0.05 -- 5% of the parent's size

UIStroke.Thickness.simple: How thick the outline is. In pixels by default (4 = a 4-pixel line), or a fraction of the parent if StrokeSizingMode is ScaledSize.

UIStroke.Transparency.simple: How see-through the outline is, separate from the object itself. 0 = solid, 1 = invisible. With TextTransparency 1 and stroke Transparency 0 you get hollow, outline-only letters.
UIStroke.Transparency.example:
local label = script.Parent.Parent -- the TextLabel the stroke is in
local stroke = script.Parent
label.TextTransparency = 1 -- hide the letter fill
stroke.Transparency = 0    -- keep the outline: hollow letters!

UIStroke.ZIndex.simple: When there are several UIStrokes on the same object, decides which one is drawn on top. Lower numbers are drawn underneath.
UIStroke.ZIndex.example:
local thick = Instance.new("UIStroke")
thick.Thickness = 8
thick.Color = Color3.fromRGB(0, 0, 0)
thick.ZIndex = 1
thick.Parent = script.Parent

local thin = Instance.new("UIStroke")
thin.Thickness = 3
thin.Color = Color3.fromRGB(255, 255, 255)
thin.ZIndex = 2 -- drawn on top of the black one
thin.Parent = script.Parent
